title: Native Sparse Attention: Hardware-Aligned Sparse Attention
one_line_claim: Hierarchical sparse attention combining token compression and blockwise selection achieves 11.6x speedup at 64k context while maintaining quality on reasoning tasks.
method_summary: NSA employs a three-branch hierarchical mechanism: blockwise token compression via residual aggregation, fine-grained token selection via learnable importance scores per block, and sliding window attention over selected tokens. Operates during inference with zero additional training.

key_findings.finding: NSA achieves 11.6x end-to-end speedup at 64k context length compared to dense attention.
key_findings.quote: NSA achieves 11.6x speedup on NVIDIA A100 at 64k context length

key_findings.finding: Perfect retrieval accuracy (100%) on needle-in-haystack at 64k context across all positions.
key_findings.quote: NSA maintains perfect (100%) accuracy on needle-in-haystack with 64k length across all needle positions

key_findings.finding: Average LongBench score of 0.469 in 32k context window, with blockwise selection outperforming uniform compression baselines.
key_findings.quote: LongBench average score reaches 0.469 under 32k context constraint

relation_to_herald.shared: Both aim to make KV-cache compression safer and more efficient for long-context generation, recognizing that uncontrolled compression causes quality degradation.
differs_on: NSA uses learned blockwise importance scoring; HERALD predicts compression-induced failures post-hoc from logit features without modifying attention.
NSA is inference-only and trainable end-to-end within the forward pass; HERALD is a separate XGBoost classifier trained offline on labelled failure data.
NSA optimizes for latency and memory bandwidth; HERALD optimizes for failure prediction horizon and intervention timing before catastrophe.
